g2p_construction.source: kokoro/pipeline.py builds en.G2P(trf=trf, british=lang_code=='b', fallback=EspeakFallback or None, unk=''); trf defaults to False; version stays None

sentence_fields.phonemes: first value returned by G2P.__call__ (tokens joined with their whitespace, unknown tokens as '')
sentence_fields.tokens: second value: the merged output tokens; phonemes null = unknown
sentence_fields.phonemes_if_default: present only when forcing DEFAULT for every POS-keyed entry changes the result (what task 5.4 will produce)

dictionary_subsets.rule: entry kept when key.lower() is a substring of a lowercased fixture word (whitespace chunk or letter/apostrophe run), or was looked up by misaki while producing this fixture (either accent run, incl. the DEFAULT run), or is a single letter
dictionary_subsets.verified: misaki re-run with the subsets gives identical output

us.rule: a token counts when its letters, lowercased, are a POS-keyed gold entry; it differs when misaki's output token differs from a run with every POS-keyed entry forced to DEFAULT (same spaCy tokens, same right-to-left context)

gb.rule: a token counts when its letters, lowercased, are a POS-keyed gold entry; it differs when misaki's output token differs from a run with every POS-keyed entry forced to DEFAULT (same spaCy tokens, same right-to-left context)

behaviours_from_en_py.unknown_word: With fallback=None, Lexicon.__call__ returns (None, None) for a word it cannot resolve: token.phonemes stays None (null in sentences.json), the token keeps its text, tag and whitespace, and G2P.__call__ writes unk ('') in the result string, so the word simply disappears from the phoneme string (the space after it stays). KPipeline.en_tokenize then turns None into ''. Inside a multi-piece word (pieces from subtokenize with no whitespace between them, e.g. a hyphenated word), the loop at en.py:668 tries the longest merge of pieces ending at the right first; an unresolvable piece stays None and merge_tokens(unk='') joins it as '', so known pieces keep their phonemes and unknown ones vanish. Words with characters outside A-Z a-z ' - (e.g. café, Wrocław) are unknown unless the exact key is in the dictionary. Pieces made only of ',-._‘’/ get ''.
behaviours_from_en_py.capitals_and_acronyms: Stress offset from case (Lexicon.__call__): lowercase None, Capitalized 0.5, ALL CAPS 2, applied with apply_stress. get_word lowercases a capitalized/ALL-CAPS word that is not itself a key when the lowercase form (or its -s/-ed/-ing stem) is known, except NNP-tagged words of 7 letters or less. is_known treats any word whose letters after the first are all upper case as known; lookup then lowercases an ALL-CAPS word that is not a gold key, and when nothing is found (or the word is NNP and its entry has no primary stress) get_NNP spells it with the gold single-letter entries, demoting all stresses to secondary and making the LAST one primary. Dotted abbreviations (U.S., Ph.D.) whose parts are at most 2 letters are also spelled by get_NNP. So the 'spell unknown ALL-CAPS' route in plan 5.5 is misaki's own rule, not a fallback.
behaviours_from_en_py.special_cases: get_special_case: 'a' -> ɐ when tagged DT else ˈA; am/an/I/by/to/in/the/used have context forms (the -> ði before a vowel; to -> tə / tʊ by next vowel; I tagged PRP -> ˌI; 'by' tagged as adverb -> bˈI; 'used' + following 'to' -> the VBD reading); 'vs' tagged IN -> versus; symbols % & + @ -> percent/and/plus/at; '.' and '/' are read 'dot'/'slash' only when spaCy tags the token ADD (URLs/e-mail). These need the part-of-speech tag (DT, PRP, IN, ADV, VBD, NNP, ADD); the Pascal port has no tagger.
behaviours_from_en_py.context: Tokens are processed right to left; TokenContext carries future_vowel (does the next word start with a vowel, None after punctuation) and future_to. A heteronym entry with a 'None' key is used when future_vowel is None, i.e. at the end of a clause; this is not a spaCy decision and the port can reproduce it.
behaviours_from_en_py.suffix_rules: Only when the whole word is not known, one level deep, stem must satisfy is_known: stem_s: -s (not -ss), -'s, -es (len>4, not -ies), -ies -> y (len>4); appends s after p t k f θ, ᵻz (US) / ɪz (GB) after s z ʃ ʒ ʧ ʤ, else z. stem_ed: -d (not -dd), -ed (len>4, not -eed); appends t after p k f θ ʃ s ʧ, ᵻd/ɪd after d, d after other non-t, and after t: GB ɪd, US ɾᵻd when the sound before t is in AIOWYiuæɑəɛɪɹʊʌ, else ᵻd. stem_ing (len>=5): stem, stem+e, or doubled consonant / -cking (drop one letter); appends ɪŋ, US t after such a vowel -> ɾɪŋ, GB returns None when the stem ends in ə or ː; stem_ing is called with stress 0.5 when the word had none. Also: word ending s' looks up word's, a trailing ' is dropped. The same _s/_ed/_ing endings apply to numbers (1990s).
behaviours_from_en_py.numbers: is_number: digits with , and . (and a leading - only at the head of a word), optional suffix ing 'd ed 's st nd rd th s. get_number: ordinal suffix -> num2words(to='ordinal'); 4-digit integer not after a currency sign -> num2words(to='year'); digits glued to letters (not head, e.g. 'B2B', '3D') -> read as digits/short groups; numbers with 2+ dots (2.0.1) -> each group, groups with a leading 0 or not of length 2 read digit by digit; $ £ € followed by a number with at most 2 decimals -> dollars/cents, pounds/pence, euros/cents ('and' between, singular for 1, pence never pluralized, zero part dropped); otherwise cardinal via num2words (float for decimals, '.5' -> point five). Commas are removed. num2words output is split on non-letters and each word looked up; the word 'and' is DROPPED ('one hundred one'), 'point' gets stress -2 (unstressed), 'minus' prefixes a leading '-'. A currency sign whose number is followed by another CD token ('$12 million') gets the plural unit appended after the number words. '¥' is not a currency. num_flags (& keep 'and', a 'a' for one, n) only come from the [n](#flags#) markdown syntax.
behaviours_from_en_py.stress: Primary ˈ and secondary ˌ are written before the vowel of the stressed syllable (restress moves an added mark to just before the first vowel after it). apply_stress(ps, s): s<-1 removes all marks; s==-1, or s in (0,-0.5) with a primary present, demotes primary to secondary; s in (0,0.5,1) with no marks adds secondary; s>=1 with only secondary promotes it; s>1 with no marks adds primary. Inside a multi-piece word, resolve_tokens demotes (-0.5) the lighter half of the pieces that carry a primary (stress_weight counts diphthong letters AIOQWYʤʧ double), unless the pieces are separated by space, '/', or mix letters and digits.
behaviours_from_en_py.post_processing: G2P version None (KPipeline's default) replaces ɾ with T and ʔ with t in every token after lookup (en.py:707), so US flaps come out as T. The dictionaries themselves contain ɾ.
behaviours_from_en_py.punctuation: Tokens tagged as punctuation by spaCy (. , -LRB- -RRB- `` '' : $ # NFP ...) keep only the characters in ;:,.!?—…"“”; ( ) map to ( ), opening quotes to “, closing to ”; a '-' or '–' tagged ':' becomes —; other symbols (*, #, [, {, <) give ''. Punctuation depends on the spaCy tag, not only on the character.
behaviours_from_en_py.other_input_syntax: G2P.preprocess honours markdown links: [word](/IPA/) sets the phonemes, [word](-1|-0.5|0.5|+1|2...) sets stress, [n](#flags#) sets number flags. A '2' between letters (P2P) is read 'to' (alias). The Pascal port may skip this syntax but should not misread brackets.
behaviours_from_en_py.chunking: KPipeline.__call__ first splits the text on \n+, then en_tokenize cuts the token list so each chunk's phoneme string is at most 510 characters, backing up to the last token whose phonemes are one of !.?…, then :;, then ,— (plus a following ) or ”), else cutting at the current token; a chunk longer than 510 is truncated with a warning.

observed_in_this_fixture.suffix_gaps: stem_ed does not undo a doubled consonant (blogged, vlogged, hashtagged, photoshopped, geotagged; GB also hummed) nor -ied -> y (photocopied), and -ed/-ing only try the stem misaki has: livestreamed, facetimed, deduped, smurfs stay unknown because livestream, facetime, dedupe, smurf are not keys. GB 'refactoring' is unknown because GB _ing refuses a stem ending in ə.
observed_in_this_fixture.capitalized_unknown_names: Capitalized unknown words (Joao, Schuler, Nguyen, Okafor) are NOT spelled: is_known only accepts words whose letters after the first are upper case, so they come out empty. Only ALL-CAPS strings are spelled.
observed_in_this_fixture.camel_case: subtokenize splits camelCase; unknown pieces vanish: 'WiFi' -> '', 'PyTorch' -> 'tˈɔɹʧ' (Py dropped).
observed_in_this_fixture.spacy_errors: spaCy's tag is sometimes wrong: 'I read books every day' -> ɹˈɛd, 'Have you read it?' -> ɹˈid, 'A is the first letter' -> ɐ (tagged DT). DEFAULT is not always worse than misaki.
observed_in_this_fixture.pos_keyed_function_words: 'that' (DT vs DEFAULT, stressed vs not) and 'IT' are POS-keyed too; 'that' is the most frequent disagreement.
observed_in_this_fixture.lead_not_heteronym: 'lead' is a plain string (lˈid) in both accents.
observed_in_this_fixture.dropped_punctuation: ' - ' with spaces (spaCy HYPH) and '--' become '' (no dash), and '--' between words leaves no space; '?—' inside 'raining?—No' is lost (one spaCy token); [ ] and < > vanish, { } become ( ); * # give ''.
observed_in_this_fixture.four_digit_numbers: Every bare 4-digit integer is read as a year (1234 -> twelve thirty four); leading zeros vanish (007 -> seven).
observed_in_this_fixture.currency_details: ¥ is not a currency (¥500 -> five hundred); $123.456 (3 decimals) is read as a plain decimal without 'dollars'; '$12 million' -> twelve million dollars.
observed_in_this_fixture.urls: '/usr/local/bin' loses 'usr'; e-mail and URL dots/slashes become dot/at only when spaCy tags them ADD.
